{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple -0.25 or 0.00 values), as models tend to overestimate prices in such regimes.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — models often overreact to recent price drops.",
    "When sentiment shifts from neutral to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 or 0.50), increase forecast bias toward higher prices, but cap upward momentum to avoid overshoot.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), reduce forecast growth rate by 20-30% to account for mean reversion or market correction.",
    "In periods with high sentiment volatility (e.g., alternating 0.00 and 0.33/0.50), apply smoothing filters to avoid erratic forecast swings.",
    "For long-term horizons (>15 days), apply a downward bias correction if recent history shows persistent price declines — models tend to overestimate recovery.",
    "When sentiment history includes 0.67 or higher, assume market is ‘overbought’ and apply a 5-10% downward adjustment to prevent overestimation of price peaks."
  ]
}
